clue.text: Group not allowed on the radio

indicators.note: words heard over the radio are only spoken, so the clue wants a word that sounds like another

parts.note: something not allowed is banned, prohibited

explanation.surface: A musical group whose records are refused airplay by broadcasters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'on the radio' about airplay, but it signals that BANNED and the answer are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a group of people, or of musicians, joined together is a band.

clue.text: Sack British concert artist, the possible end for a falling star

definitions.text: the possible end for a falling star

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job
Michael Ball is a British singer and stage performer

explanation.surface: A British concert performer is dismissed: a career ending like a star tumbling from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling star' suggests a fading celebrity, but here it is a meteor. FIREBALL is also an album by the theme band Deep Purple.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor that burns up brightly in the atmosphere is seen as a fireball, which may be the last of it.

clue.text: Germany's European record is extreme

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A German record that is the most outlandish in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Germany's' gives D, with the 's simply joining it to the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep can mean intense or extreme in degree, as in deep trouble or deep despair.

clue.text: Ant's partner fibbed about competition's close being avoided

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo, so Ant's partner is Dec

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word is placed around the letter taken next

parts.note: to fib is to tell a lie, so fibbed means lied

indicators.note: a word's close is its final letter

explanation.surface: A TV presenter lied about how a contest ended so it could be dodged.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a long-running British television double act.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to decline something is to turn it down, so declined means shunned or avoided.

clue.text: Conservative returning knighthood — is this a serious issue?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for a knight's title is read backwards

parts.note: a knighthood carries the title Sir

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician hands back their knighthood, and the media wonder if it is a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' is the surface's handing back of an honour, but it signals that SIR is read back to front as RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty, a grave problem or serious issue.

clue.text: Unfortunately, I get cold chasing a mint — sorry!

indicators.note: something chasing another comes after it, so these letters follow the earlier ones

parts.note: Polo is a brand of mint sweet with a hole in the middle

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone apologises after catching a chill running after a peppermint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges I GET and C into IGETC, which comes after A and POLO, a British brand of ring-shaped mint.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologetic person is expressing regret, saying sorry; the adjective matches the exclamation's sense.

clue.text: Clean tackles, Premier League headers by blue and red United

indicators.note: to tackle is to take hold of, so one word grips the other inside it

parts.note: clean means pure, untainted

indicators.note: headers are the heads, the opening letters of the words

explanation.surface: A football report: clean tackles and Premier League headers in a match between blue and red United sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The football words mislead: 'tackles' signals one piece taking in another, and 'headers' picks first letters. PURPLE also completes DEEP at 3 down: Deep Purple is the theme band.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple is the colour made when blue and red are combined, or united.

clue.text: Lead, helium and nitrogen escapes

indicators.note: something that escapes gets out, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry mishap: lead, helium and nitrogen gas get out of the lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal in a list of elements, but it is the verb or noun meaning to be in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead is to be at the head; a head of a group is its leader, so lead and head are synonyms.

clue.text: Boy gets diamonds for "wonderful" girl

parts.note: Al is a common short boy's name
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A young man gives his sweetheart diamonds because she is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'wonderful' point to Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's heroine of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland is the girl of that wonderland.

clue.text: Seduce EU partner with charm

indicators.note: to seduce is to lead astray, so the letters are led out of their order

explanation.surface: Win over a fellow European Union member with charm and allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seduce' reads as the main verb but signals the rearranging of EU PARTNER.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrapture is to delight intensely, to captivate or charm someone.

clue.text: Spooner urinated toys in legal documents

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial letters change places

parts.note: urinated means peed
dolls are toys

explanation.surface: A schoolboy joke: a child wets their dolls inside some official legal papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the initial P and D of PEED DOLLS gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Deed polls are legal documents, used in the UK for example to change a person's name.

clue.text: On 51p, I would get fat

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
p is the abbreviation for penny, as in 51p
I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A shopper reckons that eating on a budget of fifty-one pence would make them fat.
explanation.walkthrough: '51p' must be split: 51 is the Roman LI and p stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipids are the class of organic compounds that includes fats and oils.

clue.text: 1 + 1? Without detection, I give up …

parts.note: one is A, as in a single thing
the cross-reference to 1 down, whose solution is a word for group

indicators.note: printed in error: the setter confirmed it should read without direction, so the compass point E is removed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Faced with a puzzling sum and no clues to follow, the solver gives up and moves on to a suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'detection' is an error the setter Qaos acknowledged; 'direction' was meant, removing E (east) from ONE to leave ON. The second '1' points to 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to abandon something is to relinquish it entirely, to give up on it.

clue.text: Fool rises in the morning for tea

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot gets up early to make a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rises' means reading upwards; the surface makes it a fool getting out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea from the Indian state of the same name.

clue.text: Daughter's body clock determines when to have food

parts.note: one's body clock is an internal sense of time, an inner time

explanation.surface: A girl's internal rhythm decides the moment she gets hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'determines' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the time when a main meal is eaten is the time for dinner.

clue.text: … propose wild guess, got nothing to lose

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are set loose and rearranged
losing something means it goes, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Continuing 13: having given up, the solver proposes a wild guess, with nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' takes O from GOT leaving GT, and 'wild' rearranges GUESS plus GT.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to suggest an idea is to put it forward, to propose it.

clue.text: Sense of style

definitions.meaning: one of the five senses, alongside sight and hearing
discernment in matters of fashion and aesthetics, as in good judgment in dress

explanation.surface: A short phrase naming a feel for fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is both the sense of flavour and an eye for what is stylish.

clue.text: Room for fish, but not starter of mackerel

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a salmon is a fish

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dining room for serving fish, though mackerel is not on the starter menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' suggests a first course, but it means the first letter, M.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a reception room, especially in a grand house.

clue.text: Wearing dunce's hat, I'm a little bit slow

indicators.note: a hat sits on top, so the word's top letter is taken

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A child in the dunce's cap admits to being somewhat slow-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' means IM has D on its head: D comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim person is not very bright, slow on the uptake.

clue.text: Mineral made from two-item compound?

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture, so the letters are mixed together
two of something means the word is taken twice

explanation.surface: A chemistry question: is this mineral formed as a compound of two items?
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' rearranges ITEMITEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimetite is a lead arsenate chloride mineral, often yellow or orange.

clue.text: Abbot puts on shirt and tie

indicators.note: one piece is put on after the other, coming second

parts.note: a T-shirt, shortened to its first letter
Russ Abbot is a British comedian

explanation.surface: A monk gets dressed in a shirt and tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abbot' is not a monk but Russ Abbot, a British TV comedian; RUSS follows T.
explanation.definitionFit: To truss is to tie up tightly, as a cook trusses a bird.

clue.text: Annoyed that shirt's missing from counterfeit Man U strip

indicators.note: counterfeit means fake, so the remaining letters are rearranged
missing from means absent, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a T-shirt, shortened to its first letter

explanation.surface: A fan is angry that a fake Manchester United kit comes without its shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: MANUSTRIP loses T and 'counterfeit' rearranges the rest. Man U is Manchester United football club.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be up in arms is to be angry and protesting.

clue.text: Teachers writing about flower

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
an aster is a flower

explanation.surface: Schoolteachers composing an essay on a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' tempts as a river, something that flows, but here it is the bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools, male teachers are traditionally called masters.

clue.text: Ghost in sunglasses?

definitions.meaning: a spirit or phantom; the plural answer means more than one spirit, which the question mark excuses
a slang term for dark glasses worn against the sun

explanation.surface: A phantom wearing dark glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a ghost, and shades is slang for sunglasses.

clue.text: Rescues about 50 captives

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the letter

parts.note: rescues means saves
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Someone frees roughly fifty prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately' with 50, but it puts SAVES around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaves are people held in bondage, captives.

clue.text: Engine going about 760mph, extremely noticeable

parts.note: Mach 1, the speed of sound, is roughly 760mph

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A jet engine reaching the speed of sound, very obviously.
explanation.walkthrough: Mach 1 is written MACH I, with the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine is an apparatus with moving parts, such as an engine.

clue.text: Top worn by a barbarian

indicators.note: something worn goes around its wearer, so the word is placed around the letter

parts.note: top means best, finest

explanation.surface: A savage warrior wearing a garment on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a garment in the surface but means BEST, which goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute or savage, a barbarian, may be called a beast.

clue.text: Back massage by Norse causes skin injury

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the word reads the other way

parts.note: a massage is a rub
N is the abbreviation for Norse

explanation.surface: A back massage from a Scandinavian leaves someone hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of the body being massaged, but it reverses RUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A burn is damage to the skin caused by heat, fire or chemicals.

clue.text: Substitute every second

definitions.meaning: a replacement or stand-in, as in a back-up delegate
occurring on every other one, as in a meeting held on every other Tuesday

explanation.surface: A sports stand-in brought on at every opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a stand-in as a noun and every other one as an adjective.

clue.text: Sweet music

definitions.meaning: a hard stick-shaped sugar confection sold at British seaside resorts
a genre of popular music with a heavy beat

explanation.surface: Pleasant music.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a British sweet: a hard stick of candy with lettering through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock is both a British stick candy and a genre of loud popular music.

clue.text: Puts away chair, front to back

indicators.note: the front letter is moved to the back of the word

parts.note: a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: Someone stacks a chair, turning it front to back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts away' looks like tidying, but it means consumes food.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to put away food is to eat it heartily.

clue.text: Most cold and damp, like the largest space heard

indicators.note: heard tells you the clue wants how a word sounds, not how it is written

parts.note: the most spacious, having the most room

explanation.surface: A cellar is the chilliest and dampest, as well as the biggest room in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Rheum is watery discharge from the eyes or nose, so rheumy describes cold and damp air.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumy means watery or damp and cold, so the superlative is the most cold and damp.

clue.text: Traveller to arrive on time

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: A traveller turns up punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traveller' sounds like a person, but it is a body travelling through space.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet travels around the sun on a long orbit, a celestial traveller.
